honestBounds: The legacy Ctrl+A contact (dashboard-key.ts) and the keyed status row cannot be session-scoped: neither receives a host snapshot nor a channel, so both draw the MARKED workspace-level fallback (the Ctrl+A path reads it through readDashboardWorkflow with no id). The status row is the one surface that still NAMES another session's team on screen — measured, quoted above as a FINDING.
The durable scan (no `active` member on the service face) resolves the leadSessionId case ONLY; the single-member case is the service's own roster write path and is not reproduced here.

The real-PTY arm's latency is a FIRST-WRITE measurement of the terminal stream, not a visual-diff of a specific cell: it proves the host wrote the update then, and the per-trial capture proves the frame carried that trial's name.
The PTY arm drives the SIDEBAR and the TEAM SCENE. The merged scene and the plan scene are covered by mounted arms and by the shared reader, not by a separate PTY drive.
The board scene's team SUMMARY is scoped through the same resolver (filtered arrays into readBoardState), but it carries no scope MARKER: it is not one of the three surfaces D.2.1 enumerates.
`mpdTeams.subscribe` was consumed as a TEST DOUBLE in every in-process arm; the real implementation was exercised only through the PTY run (Lane S owns it).
verify-dist-fresh printed NO foreign staleness on this run, so there is no other lane's red to attribute here.
